plain_text:
Scientists like Christina Annunziata, M.D., Ph.D., at the
Center for Cancer Research and others at the National Cancer
Institute (NCI) are working hard to understand the ins and
outs of ovarian cancer better to help women and save lives.

plain_text:
They have learned more about the risk factors and causes
of the disease, and new ways of treating the cancer through
advanced imaging and improved early detection.
semantic_text: They have learned more about the risk factors and causes of the disease, and new ways of treating the cancer through advanced imaging and improved early detection.

plain_text:
Here are a few other key areas scientists at NCI and beyond
are studying:

plain_text:
One area of study involves the genes responsible for
ovarian cancer that family members pass on. This research
has already led to better ways to detect high-risk genes
and assess a woman's risk of developing ovarian cancer.
Scientists hope this research will also lead to new drugs that
can prevent and treat it.

help estimate how many years of life an average woman with

plain_text:
Scientists are testing new ways to screen women for ovarian
cancer with imaging techniques like functional MRIs and
PET/CT scans, as well as how drug and lifestyle changes
may alter the risk of ovarian cancer.

plain_text:
In addition to immunotherapy treatment work like that
by Dr. Annunziata, cancer researchers are exploring new
chemotherapy drugs and drug combinations that could
result in more effective treatment for ovarian cancer patients.

plain_text:
If you have or know someone with ovarian cancer or
someone who is at risk, consider joining an NCI-supported
trial near you. Learn more at NCI.gov.

plain_text:
All ovarian cancers involve one or both ovaries, or the nearby tissue that covers
organs in the abdomen (belly area). There are three types of ovarian cancers:
epithelial ovarian carcinomas, germ cell tumors, and stromal cell tumors. Each
has different characteristics and traits:

These are the most common type of
ovarian cancer. About 85% to 90% of
these cancers involve the cells that cover

organs of the pelvis and abdomen, then

women with this type of ovarian cancer

are more likely to develop this type
